_comment: Files this gate excuses TODAY, each BY NAME and with the issue that tracks it.
Measured 2026-08-12 by the fleet audit: five forks had independently grown the
same defect -- tests we wrote that no build system can reach -- and each was
found by hand. The gate is introduced with the backlog it found, because a gate
that cannot be turned on until its backlog is empty never gets turned on.
IT IS A LIST OF NAMES AND NEVER A COUNT. A count would let a new orphan hide
behind a fixed one; naming them means the gate fails the moment one MORE
appears. And an entry whose file becomes reachable is itself a failure, so a
waiver cannot quietly outlive its truth -- delete it in the commit that wires
sby is deliberately absent: it carried 33 of these until 2c2f04e wired them in.
That commit is the worked example of what every entry here needs.

OpenSTA.why: 4 C++ oracle gates: never compiled, never run.

Trilinos.why: NOT OURS, despite what `git diff --diff-filter=A` says. Both arrived in 4a5263655ee ('Restore the seven Epetra-stack packages Xyce requires'): upstream DELETED those packages and we restored them, so git reports every restored file as added by us. They are upstream's own example/benchmark helpers, at upstream's own level of wiring, and inventing a runner for them would be us maintaining a test upstream does not. Verified 2026-08-12: `git cat-file -e upstream/master:<path>` fails for both, and the adding commit is the restore.

klayout.why: 1 C++ unit test + 24 shell harnesses; the only build the fork's CI runs cannot see them.

magic.why: 9 regression gates + their generators; the audit measured that nothing runs them after a merge.

ngspice.why: the 12 vibeic_proofs gates, the fork's only regression coverage for its 17 patches.

yosys.why: two shell tests in dirs whose Makefile globs *.ys and therefore never collects *.sh.
